_doc: Reproduction record of the baseline arms (src/eval/baselines/record.py reads and writes it).
An arm may run only the (dataset, protocol) pairs listed in its own `targets` until its status is `verified`.
`published` is the number as printed in the source (a string, so the printed digits are kept);
`scale` converts our value to the printed unit (100 for a percentage). `gate: false` targets are
recorded but cannot verify an arm; `why_not_gating` says what is missing. `dataset: null` = not
runnable here. `reference_only` rows come from another paper: they authorise nothing.
Transcribed from the arXiv HTML renderings fetched 2026-10-03; nothing is quoted from memory.

vda.name: Video Depth Anything (VDA-L)
vda.settings: benchmark/infer/infer.py: input_size 518 (short side, reduced when aspect > 1.78), fp32, 32-frame windows. Data settings found by running VDA's own unmodified scripts on variants of the tree (2026-10-04, jobs 6327481, 6327549, 6327659, 6327762): Bonn = all 26 sequences (`bonn_all`, `bonn_all_500`), which is what its extractor takes; Sintel = colour files with R and B swapped on disk (`sintel_bgr`), which is what its extractor writes; ScanNet TAE over all 100 scenes, because its 20 are the first 20 of an unsorted glob and cannot be recovered.
vda.status_note: Stored measurements match the paper (15/15 within tolerance) but were taken before measured_commit existed and under the legacy '+dirty' code string, so they identify no code state; status recomputed to pending-gpu 2026-10-07. Rerun `reproduce --arm vda` at the merge commit (all datasets in one job, or split jobs at the same commit) to verify. Verified 2026-10-05 through this pipeline (jobs 6329345, 6329347): 15 of 15 gating targets. What it took, each measured with VDA's own unmodified scripts first: Bonn over all 26 sequences (bonn_all, bonn_all_500; the 5 DepthCrafter sequences give 0.0592 / 0.0821 instead of 0.053 / 0.071); Sintel on R/B-swapped colour files, as its extractor writes them (sintel_bgr 0.2981; true colours 0.3010; paper 0.295); ScanNet TAE over all 100 scenes (0.5659; paper 0.570 on an unrecoverable 20 -- the first 20 of an unsorted glob; a 20-scene mean has std 0.038). Ruled out along the way: Sintel depth encoding and depth cap; colour order for Bonn and TAE; TAE colour resolution (1296x968: 0.6020); Bonn timestamp pairing (other side of the paper: 0.0506 / 0.0681 on 5 sequences).

vda_metric.name: Metric Video Depth Anything (Metric-VDA-L)
vda_metric.paper: none: the metric models postdate arXiv:2501.12375; the only published numbers are the upstream README release notes (2025-08-28)
vda_metric.settings: as vda, with metric=True (no window alignment). The README does not state split, frame cap or alignment; ASSUMED: delta1 without alignment on the 500-frame split, TAE as eval_tae.sh.
vda_metric.status_note: Not reproduced; README protocol unrecoverable. What was established (jobs 6329352, 6329880, 6333457; upstream git history): the metric model's own inference code at the time of the README table (metric_depth/video_depth.py, 2025-08-29) is the shared code of today, aspect shrink included, and the L checkpoint on HF (2025-04-22) predates the table, so code and weights are theirs. Raw metric delta1 is 0.344-0.366 on KITTI (full frame; the aspect shrink to a 280 px short side changes the scale: median gt/pred 0.77; a 16:9 centre crop gives 0.953) and 0.5835 on our NYUv2 stills (480x640, no shrink; AbsRel 0.25, a scale error on indoor data). With a per-video scale alignment: KITTI-500 0.9218 (scale-only LSQ) / 0.9318 (median), NYUv2 0.9448 / 0.9541 -- the README's 0.910 / 0.908 sit in that range but match no single alignment, and the README's NYU is its 8-scene 500-frame video split, not built here. Undoing the shrink at full width runs out of memory on an 80 GB H100. CONSEQUENCE: this arm's absolute scale depends on input resolution and camera, so in our `metric` table it is only meaningful with the input convention stated, and not on frames wider than 16:9 uncropped.

dav.name: Depth Any Video
dav.settings: Sec. 4.2: 3 denoising steps, ensemble size 20, per-image scale+shift. The released pipeline has NO ensembling; the arm runs one pass (seed 0). The alignment space is not stated; the arm's native disparity is assumed (our `published` protocol on one-frame sequences). NYUv2 as `nyuv2_full`: the whole 480x640 frame in (a multiple of 32, so upstream's centre crop is a no-op), scored inside the Eigen crop.
dav.status_note: Not reproducible from the release: NYUv2 6.64 / 94.65 vs 5.1 / 97.0 (full 480x640 frame, Eigen crop, per-image scale+shift in disparity). One variable at a time (jobs 6329351, 6329855; offline analysis of 10 saved seeds per image): ensembling 10 seeds 6.18 / 95.12 (mean) and saturating, so the paper's ensemble of 20 does not close it; fitting in depth space as Marigold does 13.2 / 84.0; R/B-swapped input 6.81; input upscaled to 768x1024 7.41; 1 step 6.75; 10 steps 6.93. No evaluation or data code is released; the remaining candidates (the released checkpoint differing from the paper's, an unreleased ensembling/alignment procedure) cannot be tested.

ovda.name: Online Video Depth Anything (oVDA-small, context 16)
ovda.settings: The authors' own evaluation (third_party/ovda/evaluation, sent by the first author 2026-10-08), run through src/eval/ovda_paper.py: Sintel final pass with .dpt GT (23 sequences, 1064 frames); Bonn all 26 sequences, RGB/depth paired by timestamp (< 20 ms, greedy one-to-one; 29,064 pairs); KITTI the 138 data_depth_annotated/train drives, image_03 and image_02 as separate sequences (276 sequences, 85,898 frames), no crop. Only paired frames are fed; infer_video_depth(input_size=518) (fp32 here, fp16 in the paper). Their protocol: per-sequence fit of the inverse-depth prediction to 1/GT on frame 0 (ovda_first) or all frames (ovda_all), GT valid 0 < GT < limit (Sintel 10000, KITTI 255.9, Bonn 100 m) and unclipped in the fit, prediction clipped to [0, 80] m, scoring on GT < 80 m from frame 1, pixel-weighted over the dataset, delta1 <= 1.25.
ovda.status_note: Retargeted 2026-10-08 to the authors' reference evaluation. Check before the retarget: their protocol.py on our saved Sintel final-pass predictions (job 6321823) gives first-frame 0.3799 / 0.5477 and global 0.2941 / 0.6035 against the paper's 0.380 / 0.548 and 0.294 / 0.604, so our inference was right and every earlier gap was scoring and data (the 'clip GT at 80 m' match of 2026-10-04 on the clean pass was two wrong settings cancelling). Needs a GPU run: Sintel and Bonn are on Lustre; KITTI needs the raw RGB of the 138 train drives.

promptda.name: Prompt Depth Anything (ViT-L)
promptda.settings: Sec. 4.1: ARKitScenes depth-upsampling protocol (ARKitScenes paper), Validation fold (5,599 images): 192x256 ARKit depth as the prompt, laser-scan highres depth as GT, evaluated at 384x512 / 768x1024 / 1440x1920. No evaluation code is released; ASSUMED from apple/ARKitScenes depth_upsampling/dataset.py: GT nearest-resized to the evaluated size, frames rotated upright by sky_direction, L1 and RMSE in metres over GT > 0, mean over images. Inference is upstream's default (io_wrapper.load_image: long side capped at 1008, i.e. 756x1008), ONE prediction per frame, bilinearly resized to each evaluated size.
promptda.status_note: Within 5.1% on all six targets, three within tolerance (job 6322208): 384x512 0.0132 / 0.0317 vs 0.0135 / 0.0326; 768x1024 0.0131 / 0.0312 vs 0.0132 / 0.0315; 1440x1920 0.0131 / 0.0311 vs 0.0138 / 0.0316. One variable at a time on the first 20 videos (jobs 6329348, 6329881; change in L1 / RMSE vs the one-inference base): inference at each column's size +21% / +12% at 384 and +19% / +11% at 1440 (ruled out; +1.2% / +2.6% at 768); no upright rotation +21% / +10% (ruled out); R/B-swapped input +2.1% / +2.0% in every column; ARKit prompt resized to 180x240 at 1440, as Apple's x8 loader does, +2.1% / +0.5%; prediction resized nearest +1.4% / +4.2% at 384, cubic +0.1% / +1.0%; validity gt > 0.01 m: no change. The paper differs from our base by +2.3% / +2.8% (384), +0.8% / +1.0% (768), +5.3% / +1.6% (1440): no single variable gives that pattern, and none was adopted. No evaluation code is released.

runs.note: This run resized the RGB to each evaluated size before inference (378x504 for the 384x512 column). 768x1024 reproduced (0.0133 / 0.0319 vs 0.0132 / 0.0315); 384x512 did not (0.0161 / 0.0359 vs 0.0135 / 0.0326). Cause: the table's columns are evaluation resolutions of one prediction, not three inference resolutions -- upstream's loader always infers at long side <= 1008, the paper's three columns differ by under 5%, and our 768 column, the only one inferred at upstream's size, matched. Runner changed to one upstream-sized inference per frame scored at each size; rerun. No tolerance or target changed.
